detaileddescription.para: This is an attempt to get around a bug in the RWSets that come back from Qing's code. If a struct is declared inside a function, that comes back as a write to just an SgInitializedName. Which gets labeled as a local variable, sans the surrounding struct. If it's a struct variable, we only want it if it's actually in an object access, not just when it's declared. So, to figure this out, I'm going to try to check for this pattern: |___ SgBasicBlock |___ SgClassDeclaration |___ SgClassDefinition |___ SgVariableDeclaration |___ SgInitializedName

In the read/write sets a plain function call like "foo()" is basically never useful. So we take plain functions out. However, member functions and functions involved in expressions are useful. For example "a->foo()" should be in the read set. As should "a->foo().b"

Qing has started conservatively returning a->foo() as a part of the write set, on the idea that foo might modify a. But I take care of that case in TestabilityGrader, so I don't want a->foo() in the write set. (It should be in the read set though.)
